summaryText:
Guest speaker Scott Williams brought the message "Planted for Purpose" as part of Impact Church's Planted series, teaching from Ephesians 5:15-20. He began with a sports illustration about champions who do not panic after a single loss. Setbacks do not have to derail the destination God has set before us. He encouraged listeners to take honest ownership of their choices, saying "I need to be better," rather than blaming others. He also reminded the church that there is an enemy who comes to steal, kill, and destroy (John 10:10). We respect that reality without living in fear, because we already know how the story ends, and we are called to guard the ground where God has planted us.

Pastor Scott then focused on "clock management." Citing research from Christian counselor H. Norman Wright, he challenged listeners to consider how little time we may actually spend on what matters most, and urged us not to count the plays but to make the plays count. Paul wrote to believers in Ephesus, a busy and distracting city, urging them to live wisely and make the most of every opportunity. Pastor Scott offered three keys from the passage.

First, be wise. He explained that foolishness is either denying God or knowing God and choosing not to obey him. He called listeners to avoid repeated costly mistakes, to stop comparing their lives to the highlight reels of social media, and to apply what they know, since knowledge alone is not wisdom.

Second, be filled. Paul says not to be drunk on wine but to be filled with the Spirit. Being under the Spirit's influence helps us respond quickly to his prompting. Whatever we fill ourselves with shapes what we are full of. Pastor Scott encouraged people to take red flags seriously, to bring those areas to Jesus the way a coach takes a challenge to the booth, and to move from passive attendance into serving and giving.

Third, be grateful. Verses 19 and 20 call us to sing, make music from the heart, and always give thanks. Pastor Scott shared Deion Bush's testimony. Deion trusted God through the hurt of being placed on the practice squad, kept a joyful and faithful attitude, and gave God the glory when his moment came. Psalm 150:6 invites everything that has breath to praise the Lord.

The message closed with prayer for people to step into God's purpose and an invitation to surrender their lives to Jesus. Many responded, and the church celebrated together. Online viewers were encouraged to download the Impact Church app and fill out the connection card to take their next steps.
mainPoints: Be wise: make the most of every opportunity, take ownership of your choices, avoid repeating costly mistakes, and apply what you know instead of just collecting information.
Be filled with the Spirit: whatever you fill yourself with shapes your life, so stay under the Spirit's influence, respond to his prompting, and bring warning signs to Jesus.
Be grateful: praise God and give thanks in every season, trusting that he is in control, as Deion Bush's testimony showed, and step into the purpose he has planted in you.

versesMentioned.text: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.

Be very careful, then, how you live, not as unwise but as wise, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil. Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord's will is. Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery. Instead, be filled with the Spirit, speaking to one another with psalms, hymns, and songs from the Spirit. Sing and make music from your heart to the Lord, always giving thanks to God the Father for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.
Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. Praise the Lord.
Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

Monday.scripture: Ephesians 5:15-16 (NIV): Be very careful, then, how you live, not as unwise but as wise, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil.
Monday.focus: Clock management: making your days count.
Monday.action: Write down how you spent your time yesterday. Choose one time-wasting habit to reduce and one purposeful activity (prayer, reading, or time with family) to put in its place today.
Monday.prayer: Lord, help me see my time as a gift from you. Show me how to make the most of every opportunity today. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Psalm 90:12 (NIV): Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Tuesday.focus: Wisdom that comes from valuing our limited days.
Tuesday.action: Spend ten minutes asking God what he wants you to focus on this season. Write down one step you can take this week toward that purpose.
Tuesday.prayer: God, teach me to number my days. Give me a wise heart and show me the purpose you have planted in me. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Ephesians 5:17 (NIV): Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord's will is.
Wednesday.focus: Taking honest ownership and avoiding repeated mistakes.
Wednesday.action: Think of one choice or habit that keeps causing trouble. Write it down, take responsibility for it, and decide on one practical change. Consider sharing it with a trusted friend or mentor.
Wednesday.prayer: Father, give me honesty to see my own choices clearly and wisdom to change. Help me understand your will and walk in it. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Ephesians 5:18 (NIV): Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery. Instead, be filled with the Spirit.
Thursday.focus: Being filled with the Spirit instead of the things of the world.
Thursday.action: Review what you take in each day (media, conversations, habits). Replace one unhelpful input with time in Scripture or quiet prayer, and listen for the Spirit's prompting.
Thursday.prayer: Holy Spirit, fill me afresh today. Help me notice your leading and respond quickly. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Ephesians 5:19-20 (NIV): Sing and make music from your heart to the Lord, always giving thanks to God the Father for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Friday.focus: A grateful heart expressed through worship.
Friday.action: Play a worship song and sing along. Then write down five things you are thankful for and thank God for each one out loud.
Friday.prayer: Father, thank you for your goodness. Give me a heart that praises you in every season. In Jesus' name, amen.

Saturday.scripture: Psalm 150:6 (NIV): Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. Praise the Lord.
Saturday.focus: Praising God and staying planted in purpose.
Saturday.action: Take a few minutes to praise God for what he has done this week. Then reach out to someone to encourage them, and plan to serve, give, or take a next step at church this Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, I praise you with everything I have. Keep me planted in your purpose and make my days count for your glory. Amen.

title: Why You Keep Missing God’s Purpose for Your Life | Planted For Purpose
